review.summary: Mercedes lead the championship with 652 points from 20 rounds, twelve wins and 24 podiums. Andrea Kimi Antonelli tops the drivers' standings ahead of George Russell by 128 points.
review.lastRace: At the Brazilian Grand Prix both cars finished; George Russell took fourth from seventh on the grid for 12 points, while Andrea Kimi Antonelli dropped to fifth starting second and scored 10.

review.summary: Ferrari sit second with 510 points from 20 rounds, two wins and 13 podiums. Lewis Hamilton leads the pair narrowly over Charles Leclerc by 12 points across the season.
review.lastRace: At the Brazilian Grand Prix Charles Leclerc finished eighth from fourteenth on the grid for 4 points, while Lewis Hamilton dropped to ninth starting from the back of the grid and was lapped.

review.summary: Red Bull are third with 415 points from 20 rounds, three wins and 15 podiums. Max Verstappen leads a three-driver lineup well ahead of Isack Hadjar and Liam Lawson.
review.lastRace: At the Brazilian Grand Prix Max Verstappen recovered to second from twenty-first on the grid for 18 points, while Isack Hadjar took third from fifth for 15.

review.summary: McLaren are fourth with 398 points from 20 rounds, three wins and eight podiums. Lando Norris leads the pair by a wide margin over Oscar Piastri.
review.lastRace: At the Brazilian Grand Prix Lando Norris won from pole for 25 points, while Oscar Piastri finished sixth starting tenth and scored 8.

review.summary: RB F1 Team are fifth with 114 points from 20 rounds but have yet to win or reach a podium. Arvid Lindblad out-points Yuki Tsunoda comfortably this season.
review.lastRace: At the Brazilian Grand Prix Liam Lawson finished seventh from third on the grid for 6 points, while Arvid Lindblad dropped to eleventh starting eighteenth and was lapped without scoring.

review.summary: Alpine are sixth with 69 points from 20 rounds and no wins or podiums. Pierre Gasly leads the pair over Franco Colapinto.
review.lastRace: At the Brazilian Grand Prix both cars were lapped; Franco Colapinto finished thirteenth from thirteenth on the grid, and Pierre Gasly fourteenth from fifteenth, neither scoring points.

review.summary: Haas are seventh with 31 points from 20 rounds and no wins or podiums. Oliver Bearman leads the lineup well ahead of Esteban Ocon, Ryo Hirakawa and Rafael Camara.
review.lastRace: At the Brazilian Grand Prix Oliver Bearman fell to seventeenth starting sixth and was lapped without points, while Rafael Camara finished twentieth from eleventh, also without points.

review.summary: Audi are eighth with 28 points from 20 rounds and no wins or podiums. Gabriel Bortoleto and Nico Hülkenberg are level on 14 points each.
review.lastRace: At the Brazilian Grand Prix Nico Hülkenberg finished tenth from fourth for a single point though lapped, while Gabriel Bortoleto dropped to sixteenth starting nineteenth without points.

review.summary: Williams are ninth with 12 points from 20 rounds and no wins or podiums. Carlos Sainz leads the pair narrowly over Alexander Albon.
review.lastRace: At the Brazilian Grand Prix both cars were lapped; Alexander Albon finished fifteenth from ninth, and Carlos Sainz nineteenth from twelfth, neither scoring points.

review.summary: Aston Martin are tenth with just 7 points from 20 rounds and no wins or podiums. Fernando Alonso is the team's only points scorer ahead of Lance Stroll.
review.lastRace: At the Brazilian Grand Prix Fernando Alonso was lapped to twelfth starting eighth, while Lance Stroll retired from sixteenth on the grid without finishing.

review.summary: Cadillac are eleventh with zero points from 20 rounds and no wins or podiums. Both Valtteri Bottas and Sergio Pérez have failed to score this season.
review.lastRace: At the Brazilian Grand Prix Sergio Pérez was lapped to eighteenth starting twenty-second, while Valtteri Bottas did not start from seventeenth on the grid.

review.summary: Ducati lead after nineteen rounds with eight wins and sixteen podiums. Marc Marquez head their charge at the top of the riders' standings on 431 points, with Fabio Di Giannantonio second on 282; Alex Marquez, Francesco Bagnaia and Fermin Aldeguer fill out a broad midfield.
review.lastRace: In the Grand Prix of Qatar, second by Marc Marquez on 20 points, they added further scores through Fabio Di Giannantonio (8th, 8), Iker Lecuona (10th, 6), Franco Morbidelli (11th, 5) and Fermin Aldeguer (12th, 4).

review.summary: Second after nineteen rounds with nine wins and thirty-three podiums, Aprilia sit just behind Ducati. Jorge Martin sits second on 371 points, closely pursued by Marco Bezzecchi on 357; Ai Ogura and Raul Fernandez add depth below.
review.lastRace: Marco Bezzecchi won in Qatar on 25 points, leading a strong reply with Raul Fernandez third (16), Ai Ogura fourth (13) and Jorge Martin seventh (9).

review.summary: Third after nineteen rounds with two wins and eight podiums, KTM hold third behind the leading two. Pedro Acosta is their stand-out rider on 309 points, well ahead of Enea Bastianini (147) and Brad Binder (118), while Maverick Viñales has slipped down to 17th with just 17 points.
review.lastRace: Enea Bastianini took fifth in Qatar on 11 points, with Pedro Acosta sixth (10) and Maverick Viñales thirteenth (3). Brad Binder did not finish.

review.summary: Fourth after nineteen rounds with no wins and no podiums, Honda remain a step behind the top three. Luca Marini leads their riders on 117 points, ahead of Diogo Moreira (78) and Johann Zarco (63), but the rest of the grid has drifted clear.
review.lastRace: Johann Zarco took ninth in Qatar on 7 points, and Jake Dixon added two from fourteen. Diogo Moreira did not finish.

review.summary: Fifth after nineteen rounds with no wins and no podiums, Yamaha have found the season difficult. Fabio Quartararo leads on 79 points but sits behind most of the grid; Jack Miller (31), Alex Rins (29) and Toprak Razgatlioglu (18) trail well clear.

Leading the championship with 288 points, Jaguar TCS Racing hold a seventeen-point advantage over Porsche. Mitch Evans anchors their charge in fifth on 160 points, while António Félix Da Costa sits seventh on 128, giving the team a comfortable spread between its two drivers.

Second on 271 points, Porsche sit seventeen behind Jaguar with Pascal Wehrlein their strongest card, top of the driver standings on 169. Nico Müller trails in ninth on 102, so the team's total rests heavily on one driver.
Third with 252 points, Mahindra have two drivers close together in the standings. Edoardo Mortara leads the pair fifth on 137, with Nyck De Vries a handful behind in seventh on 115.
Fourth on 229 points, Andretti are carried by Jake Dennis in second on 164. Felipe Drugovich sits much further back in fourteenth on 65, leaving a wide gap between the two drivers.
Fifth with 182 points, Citroën have Nick Cassidy eighth on 114 and Jean-Éric Vergne twelfth on 68. Cassidy is the stronger of the pair by a comfortable margin.
Sixth on 157 points, Nissan rely almost entirely on Oliver Rowland fourth on 137. Norman Nato is well adrift in nineteenth on just 20.
Seventh with 152 points, Envision have Sébastien Buemi tenth on 97 and Joel Eriksson sixteenth on 55, a gap that leaves Buemi as the team's main point scorer.
Eighth on 128 points, Cupra Kiro have two drivers clustered together, Josep Maria Martí thirteenth on 66 and Dan Ticktum fifteenth on 62.
Ninth with 91 points, DS Penske are led by Taylor Barnard eleventh on 68, while Maximilian Günther sits eighteenth on just 23.
